LESSON: CHILD RIGHTS

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Social Home a) name various things found in the  Learners to identify and name 
Topic 2.1.4: Child Rights

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Child Rights. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. demonstrate responsibilities of a child in the family
2. develop a sense of responsibility for family social cohesion. on responsibilities of a child in the family.

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. demonstrate responsibilities of a child in the family
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to demonstrate responsibilities of a child in the family. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. develop a sense of responsibility for family social cohesion. on responsibilities of a child in the family.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to develop a sense of responsibility for family social cohesion. on responsibilities of a child in the family. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At school, pick litter and put it in the bin. That cares for the environment.

Example 2: Wash your hands with soap before eating and after using the toilet.

Example 3: Name two foods you eat at home that help you grow strong.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Child Rights.
2. Explain Child Rights to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Try this activity: Using stimulus materials, learners to responsibilities of a child in the family identify responsibilities of a child in the child in the family? c) develop a sense of responsibility family for family social cohesion.
4. Show that you can: demonstrate responsibilities of a child in the family
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Child Rights. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Child Rights important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Using stimulus materials, learners to responsibilities of a child in the family identify responsibilities of a child in the child in the family? c) develop a sense of responsibility family for family social cohesion.
2. In groups, learners to complete a postcard on responsibilities of a child in the family.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. demonstrate responsibilities of a child in the family
2. develop a sense of responsibility for family social cohesion. on responsibilities of a child in the family.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Learner lesson
